images.title: One array, two ways to split
images.purpose: Show that the same 27 coconuts can be split into 9 groups of 3 by the columns, or into 3 groups of 9 by the rows.
images.composition: Two copies of the same array stacked one above the other: the upper one has the columns outlined, the lower one has the rows outlined, each with a caption.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Two arrays, each of exactly 27 coconuts in 3 rows of 9 (54 coconuts in all). Each coconut is one amber #E69F00 ellipse, 56 px wide and 64 px high, with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline. In each array the column centres are 74 px apart and the row centres 84 px apart. Upper array: first column centre x 404 plus 28, spanning x 404 to 1052, rows spanning y 70 to 302. Nine teal #0072B2 rounded rectangles (3 px outline, no fill, 66 px wide and 252 px high), one around each column, so there are 9 groups of 3 coconuts. Caption under the upper array, centred at x 728 and y 350: 9 groups of 3. Lower array: spanning x 404 to 1052, rows spanning y 440 to 672. Three green #009E73 rounded rectangles (3 px outline, no fill, 664 px wide and 84 px high), one around each row, so there are 3 groups of 9 coconuts. Caption under the lower array, centred at x 728 and y 730: 3 groups of 9. All text dark #1F2937 sans-serif (40 px). No equation, no division sign and no other number in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a fact, equation, multiplication or division sign written anywhere
a number of coconuts other than 27 in each array, or a group outline that crosses two columns or two rows
images.takeaway: One array of 27 coconuts gives two ways to split into equal groups: by the columns or by the rows.
images.description: The same array of 27 coconuts twice: columns outlined as 9 groups of 3, rows outlined as 3 groups of 9.
images.context: Concept image for Two Division Facts from One Multiplication Fact. The numbers are the plan's own worked example (3 rows of 9), not a number of any book question.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student which outline makes 9 groups and which makes 3 groups. The slip to watch: thinking the two outlines count different coconuts.

image_decisions.why: The two outlined copies of one array are the mathematics of two division facts from one multiplication fact.
